title: Special Permutations
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums with n distinct positive integers, find the count of special permutations where for each pair of consecutive elements, one divides the other.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums with n distinct positive integers, find the count of special permutations where for each pair of consecutive elements, one divides the other. Return the count modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: A permutation is special when every adjacent pair has one value divisible by the other.
Use every distinct nums value exactly once.
Return the number of special permutations modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Use a bitmask for chosen indices and remember the last index.
Append an unused value only when it is divisibility-compatible with the last value.
Accumulate counts for every (mask,last), then sum all full-mask endpoints.
Every permutation has one unique sequence of prefix states, so the transitions count each valid order exactly once.
editorial: Every permutation has one unique sequence of prefix states, so the transitions count each valid order exactly once.

tests.explanation: Every pair involving one divides, while two divides four, so all six orders work.
